advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a guard test that pins the production `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` default (e.g. capture it in conftest before overriding, or parse it from `_ref_lock.py`), so the session-wide 60 s override cannot hide a change to the production bound.

Absence: `search_files('LOCAL_TIMEOUT')` under tests/ finds no assertion that pins the production value. `test_ref_lock_blob_read_budget.py:123,135` compares only to the live attribute (`{ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS}`), so it reads 60.0 in-session.
advisory.finding: The session-wide, never-restored override of `_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` to 60.0 means no in-process test runs at the production bound any more. If the production constant were changed by mistake (to 0.05 s, say, or 600 s), the whole suite would still pass. Before this change only the fixtures in two modules overrode it, and every other ref-lock test still ran at 5.0. No test asserts the production value itself.
scenarios: An edit or a mutmut mutant changes `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 5.0` to a tiny value. Production would then fail closed, treating every local ref op as HELD, but every test still passes because conftest replaced the value before any test ran.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_give_ref_lock_git_headroom`, keep the original value (e.g. `_ref_lock._PRODUCTION_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = _ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS`, or a conftest module global) before setting 60.0. Then add a unit test that asserts the captured production value is 5.0 and is below `_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS`.
